\chapter{Tests and Properties}
\chaplabel{tests}

\note{Tests and properties are not yet supported.

Examples in this chapter are not tested nor run by the interpreter.}

\note{
Ticket \#248

By default, tests actually in a given component are run.
Do not run the run function while running tests.
Overloading the same name with test and non-test functionals is not
allowed.
To test multiple components:

{\small\tt fortress test blah1.fss blah2.fss ...}
}

\note{Introduce another keyword \KWD{testhelper}
for auxiliary functions in tests.
The \KWD{testhelper} codes need to be in APIs.}

\note{
A limited form of tests are supported by the interpreter as follows:

To help make programs more robust,
the \KWD{test} modifier can appear on a top-level function definition
with type ``\EXP{() \rightarrow ()}''.
Functions with modifier \KWD{test} must not be overloaded with
functions that do not have modifier \KWD{test}.
The collection of all functions in a program that include modifier \KWD{test}
are referred to collectively as the program's \emph{tests}.
Tests can refer to non-tests but
it is a static error for a non-test to refer to any test.
Tests can refer to non-tests but non-tests must not refer to any test.

For example, we can write the following test function:
\input{\home/basic/examples/TestFactorial.tex}


When a program's tests are \emph{run},
each top-level function definition with modifier \KWD{test}
is run in textual program order.
}

Fortress supports automated program testing.
Components and APIs can declare \emph{tests}.
Test declarations specify explicit finite collections over which the
test is run.
Components, APIs, traits, and objects can declare \emph{properties}
which describe boolean conditions that the enclosing construct is expected
to obey.  Tests and properties may modify the program state.

\section{The Purpose of Tests and Properties}
To help make programs more robust, Fortress programs are allowed
to include special constructs called
\emph{tests} and \emph{properties}.  Tests consist of test data
along with code that can be run on that data.
Properties are documentation used to describe the behavior
of the traits and functions of a program; they can be thought of
as comments written in a formal language.
For each property, there is a special function that can be
called by a program's tests to ensure that the property holds for specific
test data.


A fortress includes hooks to allow programmers to run a specific test
on an executable component, and to run all tests on such a component.
A particularly useful time to run
the tests of an executable component is at component link time;
errors in the behavior of constituent components can be caught
before the linked program is run.


\section{Test Declarations}
\seclabel{test-decls}

\begin{Grammar}
\emph{TestDecl} &::=& \KWD{test} \emph{Id} \texttt[\emph{GeneratorClauseList}\texttt]
\EXP{=} \emph{Expr} \\

\emph{GeneratorClauseList} &::=& \emph{GeneratorBinding}(\EXP{,} \emph{GeneratorClause})$^*$\\

\emph{GeneratorBinding}
&::=& \emph{BindIdOrBindIdTuple}\EXP{\leftarrow}\emph{Expr} \\

\emph{GeneratorClause}
&::=& \emph{GeneratorBinding}\\
&$|$& \emph{Expr} \\

\emph{BindIdOrBindIdTuple}
&::=& \emph{BindId}\\
&$|$& \texttt{(} \emph{BindId}\EXP{,} \emph{BindIdList} \texttt{)}\\

\end{Grammar}

A test declaration begins with
\KWD{test} followed by an identifier, a list of zero or more generators
(described in \secref{generators}) enclosed in square brackets, the
token \EXP{=}, and a subexpression.
When a test is \emph{run} (See \secref{basicops}), the
subexpression is evaluated in each extension of the enclosing environment
corresponding to each point in the cross product
of bindings determined by the generators in the generator list.

For example, the following test:
\note{The fortify has some problems here...}
\begin{Fortress}
{\tt~}\pushtabs\=\+\( \KWD{test} \VAR{fxLessThanFy}[{x \leftarrow E}, {y \leftarrow F}] = \VAR{assert} (f(x) < f(y))\)\-\\\poptabs
\end{Fortress}
checks that, for each value $x$ supplied by generator $E$,
and for each value $y$ supplied by generator $F$,
\EXP{f(x)} is less than \EXP{f(y)}.

andRel[\E\](p: Gen[\E\] -> RelCondG[\E\], q: Gen[\E\] -> RelCondG[\E\]): Gen[\E\] -> CondG[\E\] =
  fn (g: Gen[\E\]): CondG[\E\] => BothOf[\E\](p(g), q(g))

combine[\E\](p: Gen[\E\] -> CondG[\E\], q: Gen[\E\] -> CondG[\E\]): Gen[\E\] -> CondG[\E\] =
  typecase p of
    rp:(Gen[\E\] -> RelCondG[\E\]) =>
      typecase q of
        rq:(Gen[\E\] -> RelCondG[\E\]) => andRel[\E\](rp, rq)
        else => q
      end
    else => p
  end

applyRel[\E\](p: Gen[\E\] -> CondG[\E\], g: Gen[\E\]): String =
  typecase p of
    rp:(Gen[\E\] -> RelCondG[\E\]) => "rel arrow: " || rp(g).descr()
    else => "cond arrow: " || p(g).descr()
  end

pickZ(p: ZZ32 -> CondG[\ZZ32\]): String =

(* An object that extends a generic trait at the static argument Any runs the trait's methods at Any. *)
component ExtendsGenericAtAnyCompiled
export Executable

trait Holder[\T extends Any\]
  keep(x: T): T = x
  label(): String
end

object AnyHolder extends Holder[\Any\]
  label(): String = "any"
end

isZZ32(x: Any): Boolean = typecase x of
    ZZ32 => true
    else => false
  end

isString(x: Any): Boolean = typecase x of
    String => true
    else => false
  end

run(): () = do

end

end

cat > compiler_tests/ForbidClauseCompiled.fss <<'EOF'
(* A forbid clause throws on, as a ForbiddenException chained to it, an exception of a listed type that no catch clause took; a catch clause takes its exception first, and one of no listed type passes on. *)
component ForbidClauseCompiled
export Executable

object Boom extends UncheckedException end
object Bang extends UncheckedException end
object Fizz extends CheckedException end

boom(): () = throw Boom
bang(): () = throw Bang
fizz(): () = throw Fizz

chainName(x: Exception): String = typecase x of
    Boom => "Boom"
    Bang => "Bang"
    Fizz => "Fizz"
    else => "other"
  end

(* Boom, which the forbid clause lists, is thrown on as a ForbiddenException whose chain is Boom. *)
forbidden(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      boom()
    forbid Boom
    end
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)
    Boom => seen := "Boom passed on"
  end
  seen
end

(* The forbid clause lists a supertype of Bang, beside a type of no match. *)
forbiddenBySupertype(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      bang()
    forbid { CheckedException, UncheckedException }
    end
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)
    Bang => seen := "Bang passed on"
  end
  seen
end

(* A catch clause that matches takes the exception before the forbid clause. *)
caughtFirst(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      boom()
    catch e
      Boom => seen := "caught Boom"
    forbid Boom
    end
  catch f
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(f.chain)
  end
  seen
end

(* A catch clause that does not match leaves the exception to the forbid clause. *)
catchMissesForbidTakes(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      boom()
    catch e
      Bang => seen := "caught Bang"
    forbid Boom
    end
  catch f
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(f.chain)
    Boom => seen := "Boom passed on"
  end
  seen
end

(* An exception of no listed type passes on as it is. *)
passesOn(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      fizz()
    forbid { Boom, Bang }
    end
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)

(* A forbid clause throws on, as a ForbiddenException chained to it, an exception of a listed type that no catch clause took; a catch clause takes its exception first, and one of no listed type passes on. *)
component ForbidClauseCompiled
export Executable

object Boom extends UncheckedException end
object Bang extends UncheckedException end
object Fizz extends CheckedException end

boom(): () = throw Boom
bang(): () = throw Bang
fizz(): () = throw Fizz

chainName(x: Exception): String = typecase x of
    Boom => "Boom"
    Bang => "Bang"
    Fizz => "Fizz"
    else => "other"
  end

(* Boom, which the forbid clause lists, is thrown on as a ForbiddenException whose chain is Boom. *)
forbidden(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      boom()
    forbid Boom
    end
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)
    Boom => seen := "Boom passed on"
  end
  seen
end

(* The forbid clause lists a supertype of Bang, beside a type of no match. *)
forbiddenBySupertype(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try
    try
      bang()
    forbid { CheckedException, UncheckedException }
    end
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)
    Bang => seen := "Bang passed on"
  end
  seen
end

caughtFirst(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"

    forbid Boom

  catch f
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(f.chain)
  end
  seen
end

(* A catch clause that does not match leaves the exception to the forbid clause. *)
catchMissesForbidTakes(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"
  try

    catch e
      Bang => seen := "caught Bang"
    forbid Boom
    end
  catch f
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(f.chain)
    Boom => seen := "Boom passed on"
  end
  seen
end

passesOn(): String = do
  seen: String := "none"

    forbid { Boom, Bang }
    end
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)
    Fizz => seen := "Fizz passed on"
  end
  seen
end

  end
  seen

content.content:
## B.9 The compiler tail

`CodeGenerationPhase` runs, per component, a `FreeVariables` pass, a `FreeVarTypes` pass and a `ParallelismAnalyzer`, then `CodeGen` (`phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java:183-196`).

`CodeGen`'s constructor opens the output jar immediately — `NamingCzar.cache + <dotted component name> + ".jar"` in `bytecode_cache` (`codegen/CodeGen.java:391-393`, `compiler/NamingCzar.java:132`) — which is why a failed compile leaves a truncated jar behind.

Classes are written with ASM `COMPUTE_FRAMES` through `CodeGenClassWriter`/`ManglingClassWriter` (`CodeGen.java:406`); generic declarations are emitted once as templates, to be stamped out at load time (B.11).

For apis that were synthesized from `import java`, the same phase asks `ForeignJava` to generate wrappers (`CodeGenerationPhase.java:94`, `repository/ForeignJava.java:757,807` → `compiler/nativeInterface/FortressTransformer.java:37`), which writes them into `nativewrapper_cache` (`FortressTransformer.java:33`).

There is no link step that produces a single artifact: `fortress compile` leaves jars, and `fortress run` finds them by classpath.

`fortress link` and `fortress build` differ from `compile` only in passing `doLink=true` (`Shell.java:1063`), which makes the repository add the library *components* to the graph (`GraphRepository.java:883-902`) — that is, in principle, the single command that compiles the world in the right order, as opposed to the hand-ordered recipe in `repo-internals.md:170-180`.

content.content:
# The library

The library is `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`, without the compiler's own files there:

- In `Library/`: the interpreter's prelude, `FortressLibrary.fss` and `.fsi`, and its other components. The compiler's `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra` and `CompilerSystem` are not part of it. `FortressAst.fss` and `.fsi` are generated from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`: edit that file, never these two.
- In `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`: `FortressBuiltin`, `NativeArray` and the rest. The compiler's `CompilerBuiltin` is not part of it.
- `LibraryBuiltin/AnyType`, the top type, belongs to both libraries. After an edit to it, also take the compiled path's step (`build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library").
- `Library/incomplete/` is not on the source path (`default_repository/configuration`), so no program can import what it declares. Nothing that the suites or the model program run imports `Library/GeneratorLibrary.fss` either. Before you cite a declaration as the library's way, check that a running program can reach it.

## How loops and reductions call the library

The desugarer, which both paths share, turns these forms into calls of the library:

- `for x <- g do b end` becomes `g.loop(fn x => b)`, a call of the generator's `loop` method. Each further generator nests one more `loop` call inside.
- `while x <- e do b end` becomes `while __whileCond(e, fn x => b) do end`. `if x <- e then ... end` becomes a call of `__cond`.
- A comprehension or a big operator, such as `SUM`, becomes a call of `__bigOperator`, whose argument calls `__generate` on each generator. So does a big operator inside another: no desugaring calls the library's `__bigOperator2`.

These functions work on the library's generators and reductions: `trait Generator` and `trait Reduction` in `FortressLibrary.fsi`, and `RangeInternals.fss` for ranges. `FortressLibrary.fss` also defines `__loop`, but no desugaring calls it. So a failure inside a loop or a reduction is most often in the library's code, and its fix is a library edit.

## The curator's decisions on the library

- Scalar ranges are over `ZZ32` only. A range over another integer type is a static error, and walk stops when it builds one. Write a wider counter as a `ZZ32` loop that widens its index.
- `ZZ32` and numerals convert into `RR64` implicitly. `ZZ64` converts into `RR64` only explicitly, by `asFloat`.
- For arithmetic that wraps on overflow, use the wrapping operators ∔ `DOTPLUS`, ∸ `DOTMINUS` and ⨰ `DOTTIMES`. Parenthesise every such expression fully, because their precedence is stated only among themselves.
- `SUM` and `PROD` are generic over `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing`. Write the element type wherever generators stand in brackets, also where the generators, the body or a declared type fix it: `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#n] f(j)`. The checker refuses a call without it (ledger row 731). Walk runs such a call at its value's declared type, or else at the join of its elements' run-time types. An empty `SUM` with no static argument written and no declared type gives the integer 0, and an empty `PROD` the integer 1, whatever the body's type (ledger row 716). With a static argument written that is not a number type, such as a user group, an empty or filtered `SUM` ends in `CastError` (ledger row 436).
- An indexed type's index parameter is bounded by `Index` (`revival-changes.md`, "Traits and objects"). `BoundedRange[\I\]` cannot take the bound, because the open range `(:)` stays a range over `Any` (P-56). So its `atMost(n: I): FullRange[\I\]` has the condition `where { I extends Index }`, which each call must meet (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`). A type whose static parameter is a range's index type takes the bound too, as `UniformDistribution[\T extends Index\]` over a `FullRange[\T\]` (`Library/Random.fsi`).
- An array's `fill` takes a value, and its `tabulate` a function of the index: `array[\ZZ32\](4).fill(0)`, `array[\ZZ32\](4).tabulate(fn (i:ZZ32):ZZ32 => 10 i)`. The factories that take a function are `tabulatedArray1` to `tabulatedArray3` and `tabulatedVector`.

## Designing a change

## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

## Comparing with an earlier run

- `ant testSystem` runs in four shards, the summary's rows `system-0` to `system-3`. A shard takes the files by their place in a sorted list, so an added file moves every later file to another shard. When you compare by hand, compare only the sum of the four. `gate_compare` sums them.
- In printed output, mask only these differences: the `Operation took <n>ms` line, a Java line number in a stack frame, an object's identity hash (`@` and hex digits), and a position in a library file that your change moved. In your report, list each test with a masked difference, and the kinds masked in it.
- If your brief asks you to compare the interpreter tests with a base run, use the two scripts in `explorations/coordinator/tools/count-run/`. `count-run.sh` runs every `ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss` under walk, one JVM per test: run it once on the base commit and once after your edit. `compare-normalised.py` compares the two runs, with the last three masks above. Each script's header gives its usage.

(* A forbid clause throws on, as a ForbiddenException chained to it, an exception of a listed type that no catch clause took; a catch clause takes its exception first, and one of no listed type passes on. *)
component ForbidClauseCompiled
export Executable

object Boom extends UncheckedException end
object Bang extends UncheckedException end
object Fizz extends CheckedException end

boom(): () = throw Boom
bang(): () = throw Bang
fizz(): () = throw Fizz

chainName(x: Exception): String = typecase x of
    Boom => "Boom"
    Bang => "Bang"
    Fizz => "Fizz"
    else => "other"
  end

(* The forbid clause lists Boom. *)
forbidBoom(): () = do
  try
    boom()
  forbid Boom
  end
end

(* The forbid clause lists a supertype of Bang, beside a type of no match. *)
forbidBySupertype(): () = do
  try
    bang()
  forbid { CheckedException, UncheckedException }
  end
end

(* A catch clause that matches takes the exception before the forbid clause. *)
catchBeforeForbid(seen: String): String = do
  s: String := seen
  try
    boom()
  catch e
    Boom => s := "caught Boom"
  forbid Boom
  end
  s
end

(* A catch clause that does not match leaves the exception to the forbid clause. *)
catchMissesForbidTakes(): () = do
  try
    boom()
  catch e
    Bang => println("caught Bang")
  forbid Boom
  end
end

(* An exception of no listed type passes on as it is. *)
forbidOthers(): () = do
  try
    fizz()
  forbid { Boom, Bang }
  end
end

(* A body that completes normally ignores the forbid clause. *)
completesNormally(): String = do
  s: String := "none"
  try
    s := "body"
  forbid Boom
  end
  s
end

(* What a call of f throws, as the caller's catch clause sees it. *)
outcome(f: () -> ()): String = do
  seen: String := "nothing thrown"
  try
    f()
  catch e
    ForbiddenException => seen := "forbidden " || chainName(e.chain)
    Boom => seen := "Boom passed on"
    Bang => seen := "Bang passed on"
    Fizz => seen := "Fizz passed on"
  end
  seen
end

run(): () = do
  assert(outcome(forbidBoom), "forbidden Boom", "try.tex, section \"Try Expressions\": a listed type gives a ForbiddenException chained to the thrown exception")
  assert(outcome(forbidBySupertype), "forbidden Bang", "try.tex, section \"Try Expressions\": a subtype of a listed type gives a ForbiddenException")
  assert(catchBeforeForbid("none"), "caught Boom", "try.tex, section \"Try Expressions\": an exception matched by both clauses is caught by the catch clause")

  assert(outcome(forbidOthers), "Fizz passed on", "try.tex, section \"Try Expressions\": an exception matched by no clause completes the try abruptly")
  assert(completesNormally(), "body", "try.tex, section \"Try Expressions\": a try block that completes normally ignores the forbid clause")
  println("PASS")
end

end

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                adds TEXT to row N's notes, before the row's own
                             "full text: history, row N" marker where it has
                             one, else at their end (notes of `none` are
                             replaced); checks the notes cell and the row's
                             length only, so a failure in another cell does
                             not block it; a row keeps its own cells
  rewrite N FILE             FILE holds row N's whole new line (its # cell N
                             or ?, or the seven cells after it); checks it
                             against the template and writes it in the row's
                             place, its earlier line in the history
                             ("rewritten"): the route that corrects a claim,
                             cuts notes, or moves a reproducer. A FIXED or
                             DUPLICATE row stays so (a FIXED row's commit is
                             checked); a row becomes one only by close or
                             duplicate
  close N --commit HASH --test NAME [--settled TEXT] [--note TEXT] [--claim C]

SKEPTIC.md
### G (`rung-codegen-where`, `c324b841c`)

**The change.** The team's code generator refuses a function, method, object or trait declaration whose own header carries a `where` clause: each of the guards of `forFnDecl`, `forObjectDeclPrePass` and `forTraitDecl` requires `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:2936`, `:4075`, `:4982` at the team's last commit `a874948ac`), so `fortress compile` stops with 'Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl.' or 'Can't compile TraitDecl …'/'Can't compile ObjectDecl …'. What the tree now does: it compiles such a declaration, and emits nothing for the clause, whose constraints the checker has checked; a call of a function or method whose clause introduces a `where`-clause variable dies at run time (row 867); a function or method with a contract is still refused (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/WhereBoundFunctionCompiled.fss`, `WhereBoundMethodCompiled.fss`, `WhereBoundObjectCompiled.fss`, `WhereBoundTraitMethodCompiled.fss`, `ComprisesWhereFunctionalMethodCompiled.fss`; `XXXFunctionContractCodeGeneration.fss`). The reason, as evidence: the specification lets a declaration carry the clause, "Static parameters may have constraints placed on them in a \KWD{where} clause." and "Object or functional declarations may include \KWD{where} clauses" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:332-333`, `:497`); the clause only constrains static parameters, which the checker checks and the run time does not see; and the library carries such clauses (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3449`, `:3451`, `:4114`; `Library/List.fss:87`; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss:24`), which the code generator refused while the checker passed them, measured as 'Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl. node = g[\U\](u:U):String' on a program of that form.

**Provenance.** P-151, "Only the `where`-clause forms that the team wrote down are built" (its "Row 701: the code generator's half."); the phase 3 exit judgement's item 9, its default a named code-generator rung before the names batch, the coordinator's call; climb batch 24's forks 12 (the `where` half only, nothing emitted, the contract condition kept) and 13 (the tests); climb batch 24, rung G, rung-codegen-where.

The runs were in three worktrees seeded detached at `dc571c1f3` from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base25`, whose code is `25238e60c`'s, after its build, library order and walk run had ended at 00:41 UTC on 2026-11-02 and before its marker `tmp/BUILT` was written at 01:28: `/home/user/fortress-p25` (the code generator's runs, then the samples of N, D and P with the `asFloat` control), `/home/user/fortress-p25t` (the texts of R, U and A, then the order of application) and `/home/user/fortress-p25patch` (the six texts and samples together, built). Machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` for the stages and the direct runs; two other workers shared the machine, the load from 0.3 to 5, so no time here is one to compare, and walk was not timed.

## The files

- `count.sh`: F-32's classes counted again on a built tree, made from `plan-24/probes/count.sh`: the natives probe's scripts read from `4a46fb83a`, with `plan-24/probes/remap.py` run on climb batch 24's table of its base, so that each of the 173 bindings that name a helper gets the glue class it named before it moved; then `plan-23/probes/movable.py`, then the column `now`. Writes `classified.tsv`, `movable.tsv`, `moved.tsv` and `helpers-javap.txt`; it reads the tree and builds nothing, so it was run on the base build itself.
- `classified-base.tsv`, `moved-base.tsv`: `count.sh`'s output on the base build. The first equals climb batch 24's `plan-24/probes/classified-base.tsv` binding for binding, line numbers included; the second lists the 173 bindings that name helpers, each with the glue class it named before it moved. Rungs A and U change six `asFloat` headers, from `Float` to `RR64`, so the next planner's `remap.py`, which matches by file, owner and header, must match those six by file and line, which their one-line edits keep.
- `n3.py` and `n3-base.tsv`: N3's 158, the class C bindings of `classified.tsv`, one line a binding with its line, owner, header, glue class, the batch's rung or the home of what it waits on, the helper's Java signature, the types the compiled checker reads it at in walk's world, whether microGPT's lines reach it, and the glue class's computation read from `interpreter/glue/prim/`. Its last lines, on standard error, count each rung.
- `codegen.sh` and `cgkinds.py`: the code generator over the distance stage's fourteen components, declaration by declaration, on the tree at `$FORTRESS_HOME`: the distance stage's shadows and driver (`tools/distance/`) with `-order full` and the flags of the probe of 2026-10-23 (`perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, section 1), whose own scripts were not kept. `cgkinds.py` counts each refused declaration once, at its first wall, by component and by the code generator's message. About 140 s on the base, 210 s with the helper strings on glue classes.
- `apply25.py`: writes a rung's text, or the planner's sample of one, into a tree at the base, by exact text, each edit matching once: `R`, `U` and `A` the whole texts; `N`, `D` and `P` the samples; `asfloat-control` `Int`'s `asFloat` moved at its header `Float`.
- `rung-R.patch`, `rung-U.patch`, `rung-A.patch`: `apply25.py`'s three texts on a clean checkout of the base, taken with `git diff`. `sample-D.patch`, `sample-P.patch`, `sample-N.patch`: its three samples, likewise. Each applies to the base alone (`git apply --check`), and the six one after another in the gather's order D, P, A, R, U, N through `git apply --3way`.

## How to run them again

From a worktree seeded from a base build at the batch's base, set up as the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md` says:

    explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/count.sh $PWD tmp/count
    python3 -B explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/n3.py tmp/count/classified.tsv ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim > tmp/n3.tsv
    explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/codegen.sh tmp/cg                     # in the background; prints the table
    python3 -B explorations/compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/apply25.py $PWD R U A      # or: git apply --3way the patches in the gather's order
    ant compileAll        # then the library order, before a compiled test
    explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/distance.txt tmp/distance        # in the background
    explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/count.txt tmp/count-scratch # in the background
    ant testSystem; ant testSpecData                                                   # in the background

The control of the code generator's run puts the 173 helper strings back on their glue classes for one run, from `tmp/count/moved.tsv` (`glue_before`, `helper_now`), the string searched from the header's line through three lines after it, since a header can span two lines. The `asFloat` control is `apply25.py <tree> asfloat-control` with the distance stage after it.

The value probes were scratch programs, not kept, each run on the old code (`tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base25 <tree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss`) and on the text (`bin/fortress P.fss`), their outputs compared with `diff`: `ValR`, R's ten at the bounds and at pairs of signs; `ValU`, `UnsignedLong`'s getters and `NN64`'s prefix `DOTMINUS` at seven values, and `NN32`'s `CHOOSE` at 128 pairs, each overflow caught; `ValA`, the six `asFloat`s at their bounds; `ValN`, `ValD` and `ValQ`, the samples of N, D and P; `ZeroZZ32`, `ZeroZZ64`, `ZeroNN32`, `ZeroNN64` and `ZeroZZ`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero in a `try` catching `DivisionByZero`. Each was a do-block of typed bindings and `println` lines, written by a script: a list literal at a declared `List[\ZZ32\]` is an `ArrayList[\Int\]` under walk and does not bind (row 364's kind), so the lists were left out. The compiled sample, `SampleRUACompiled` and `SampleNDQCompiled`, each with a `.test` of `link`, `run` and `run_out_contains=PASS`, ran through `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh samples ProjectFortress/compiler_tests SampleRUACompiled.test SampleNDQCompiled.test` after the library order on
#!/bin/bash
# codegen.sh <out-dir>: the code generator over the one library's components, declaration by declaration, on the
# tree at $FORTRESS_HOME (climb batch 25's planner), made from the probe of 2026-10-23
# (perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md, sections 1 and 3, whose run.sh and classify2.py were not kept): the
# distance stage's own shadows, made from the tracked sources at this run (tools/distance/shadow-patch.py and
# add-patch.py), and its driver, DistanceMulti, run with -order full (every compiler phase, code generation among
# them) and -setting compile, the compile command's own setting, which the distance stage runs (its run.sh), over
# the stage's fourteen components in its order. The report's flags: -Dprobe.tolerant=true (the checker checks each
# declaration apart and its errors stop nothing; code generation catches each declaration's failure),
# -Dprobe.bottomCompare=true, -Dprobe.skipOverloads=true (no dispatch methods), the overloading memo off.
# Writes <out-dir>/run.txt and prints the classified table (cgkinds.py). One JVM, -Xmx4g; about 200 s on an idle box.
set -u
O=$(mkdir -p "$1" && cd "$1" && pwd)
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance"
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss
 Library/CovariantCollection.fss Library/OneShotFlag.fss"
rm -rf "$O/shadow-src" "$O/shadow-classes" "$O/classes" "$O/caches" "$O/tmp"
mkdir -p "$O/shadow-src" "$O/shadow-classes" "$O/classes" "$O/caches" "$O/tmp"
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$O/shadow-src" \
           && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$O/shadow-src" ) > "$O/shadows.txt" 2>&1 || { echo "shadows stale"; exit 1; }
javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$O/shadow-classes" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
    "$O/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$O/shadows.txt" 2>&1 || { echo "shadows do not compile"; exit 1; }
javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$O/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$O/shadows.txt" 2>&1 || exit 1
S=$(date +%s)
( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
      -Djava.io.tmpdir="$O/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$O/caches" \
      -Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.bottomCompare=true -Dprobe.skipOverloads=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false \
      -cp "$O/shadow-classes:$O/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order full -setting compile $COMPONENTS ) > "$O/run.txt" 2>&1
echo "rc=$? seconds=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))" >> "$O/run.txt"
rm -rf "$O/caches" "$O/tmp"
python3 -B "$HERE/cgkinds.py" "$O/run.txt"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Climb batch 25's planner: the code generator's refusals in a codegen.sh run, by component and by kind.
A declaration counts once, at its first wall: an @@CG FAIL line of the declaration loop, an @@CG PREFAIL line of the
object pre-pass, or an @@CG CTORFAIL line of CodeGen's constructor (inherited methods). Its kind is the code
generator's message, or, where the message is null, the exception's class and the frame that threw, as the probe of
2026-10-23 named them (perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md, section 1, "Classifier"). The component is the one
whose ### target line came last before the line. Usage: cgkinds.py run.txt [--list]"""
import re, sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
lines = open(sys.argv[1], errors='replace').read().split('\n')
comp, rows, ok, compfail = '?', [], Counter(), []
for l in lines:
    m = re.match(r'^### target (\S+)', l)
    if m: comp = m.group(1).split('/')[-1].replace('.fss', ''); continue
    if l.startswith('@@CG OK\t'): ok[comp] += 1; continue
    if l.startswith('@@CG COMPONENT-FAIL'): compfail.append((comp, l)); continue
    for tag in ('@@CG FAIL\t', '@@CG PREFAIL\t', '@@CG CTORFAIL\t'):
        if l.startswith(tag):
            p = l.split('\t')

(`test stringifyChars`; row 823) (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-25.md:375-385; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5795-5796, :2029-2030, :2897-2899 at 97a416b18)

## 1. What changed, and why

Three changes in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, and one helper that the second needs, nothing else of the original tree:

- `generateTypeReference`, its `AnyType` branch (base `:5795-5796`, now `:5845-5851`): it was empty and fell through to the throw 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (base `:5802`). It now calls `generateTypeReference` with Any's own name, `NodeFactory.makeId(span, WellKnownNames.anyTypeLibrary(), WellKnownNames.anyTypeName)`, and no static arguments, and continues, as the `TraitType` branch does for a trait (`:5835-5837`). For a name without static arguments the method emits `GETSTATIC <its RTTI class>.ONLY` (`:5759-5767`), here `fortress/AnyType$Any$RTTIc.ONLY`, the field that the bootstrap class declares (`ProjectFortress/src/fortress/AnyType.java`, `RTTIc.ONLY`). The `BottomType`, `SelfType` and `AbbreviatedType` branches stay empty, each still ending in the throw (`:5833-5834`, `:5843-5844`, `:5852-5853`, throw `:5857`).
- `forTry` (base `:2019-2073`, now `:2019-2087`): the throw 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (base `:2029-2030`) is gone. After the catch clauses, which are unchanged, each type of the forbid clause is tested in turn, as a catch clause tests its type (`DUP`, `FException.getValue`, `InstantiatingClassloader.generalizedInstanceOf`, `IFEQ`); on a match the exception's value is passed to `throwForbiddenException`. The rethrow (`ATHROW`) and the label `done` move out of the `if (catchClauses.isSome())` block (`:2041`, `:2078-2081`) and are emitted when the try has a catch clause or a forbid clause, so a try with neither emits what it emitted before.
- `throwForbiddenException` (new, `:2089-2122`): with the exception's value on the stack, it finds `ForbiddenException`'s constructor in the api index of `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()` (the component's own index when it is that library), takes its parameter type and its result, casts the value to the parameter's class, calls the constructor's static method through `idToPackageClassAndName` and `NamingCzar.jvmMethodDesc`, as a source call of `ForbiddenException(e)` is emitted, wraps the result in an `FException` as `forThrow` does (`NEW`, `DUP_X1`, `SWAP`, `INVOKESPECIAL`) and throws it. The api's own types are named unqualified in its index, so the descriptor is made with the library's api as the default: with the program's api the first run asked for `ForbidClauseCompiled$ForbiddenException.class`, 'Resource not found'. The emitted call is the source call's, `invokestatic fortress/CompilerLibrary.ForbiddenException:(Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$Exception;)Lfortress/CompilerLibrary$ForbiddenException;` (by `javap -c -p` on the test's jar, the same instruction as a probe's source `throw ForbiddenException(e)` compiled on the base).
- `fnDeclCompilableModifiers` (base `:2897-2899`, now `:2947-2949`): `.combine(Modifiers.Test)`, so `forFnDecl`'s guard (`:3021`) passes a function declared `test`, which then compiles as the function it is. What `fortress test` runs is not changed.

REPORT.md sections 1, 2.
2. **The code generator compiles a `try` with a `forbid` clause as the specification gives it.** Holds after `<C>`: an exception that the body throws and that no catch clause takes, of a type the clause lists or below it, is thrown on as a `ForbiddenException` whose `chain` is that exception; the catch clause takes first; an exception of no listed type passes on unchanged; a normal completion ignores the clause (`Specification/basic/expressions/try.tex:47-53`, `:56-81`; `Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:177-210`). `forTry` tests the forbid types after the catch clauses (`CodeGen.java:2064-2081`) and a new `throwForbiddenException` (`:2089-2122`) calls the library's constructor, found in the api index of `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()`, as a source call `ForbiddenException(e)` is emitted. # Rung C (`rung-codegen-walls`): the code generator's three walls: `Any` in an `extends` clause, `forbid`, and `test`

problem: under the switch-over's setting the code generator refused 50 declarations of the one library's fourteen components in 14 kinds, three of them in one method each of `CodeGen.java`: 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (`MIMapReduceReduction`, `TrivialOpenRange`; row 820), 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (`shouldRaise`; row 821) and 'Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl.' (`test stringifyChars`; row 823) (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-25.md:375-385; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5795-5796, :2029-2030, :2897-2899 at 97a416b18)
spec: a forbid clause throws "a new ForbiddenException ... with the thrown exception as its argument", the catch clause first (Specification/basic/expressions/try.tex:56-81), the same as a catch clause that throws ForbiddenException(e) (Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:177-210); an extends clause names any instance of a generic trait, Any among the static arguments (Specification/basic/traits.tex, "Trait Declarations"); the test modifier on a top-level function (Specification/basic/tests.tex:36-55, its note)
precedent: the IntArg branch of the same `generateTypeReference`, which repaired the same message for a size (row 411, e893a3e00; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5863-5873); `forTry`'s own catch-clause loop and `forThrow` (:2047-2063, :2006-2017); the source call of a library constructor (`functionalRefToPackageClassAndMethod`, `resolveMethodAndSignature`, :3841-3857, :1492-1515); the trait guard that already holds `test` (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/Modifiers.java:146-147)
deviation: the AnyType branch builds Any's name (`AnyType.Any`) and calls `generateTypeReference`, where the TraitType branch passes the trait type's own name (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5845-5851); the ForbiddenException call is emitted by a new private helper, `throwForbiddenException`, which finds the constructor in the library's api index, as no source call names it (:2089-2122); the guard admits `test` on methods as well as on top-level functions, where the specification's note speaks of top-level functions (:2947-2949); nothing else departs from the specification's spelling (none)
historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java (the team's sites at a874948ac: `forTry`'s throw :2013-2014, the guard :2866-2868, the AnyType branch :5753-5754)

## 1. What changed, and why

Three changes in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, and one helper that the second needs, nothing else of the original tree:

- `generateTypeReference`, its `AnyType` branch (base `:5795-5796`, now `:5845-5851`): it was empty and fell through to the throw 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (base `:5802`). It now calls `generateTypeReference` with Any's own name, `NodeFactory.makeId(span, WellKnownNames.anyTypeLibrary(), WellKnownNames.anyTypeName)`, and no static arguments, and continues, as the `TraitType` branch does for a trait (`:5835-5837`). For a name without static arguments the method emits `GETSTATIC <its RTTI class>.ONLY` (`:5759-5767`), here `fortress/AnyType$Any$RTTIc.ONLY`, the field that the bootstrap class declares (`ProjectFortress/src/fortress/AnyType.java`, `RTTIc.ONLY`). The `BottomType`, `SelfType` and `AbbreviatedType` branches stay empty, each still ending in the throw (`:5833-5834`, `:5843-5844`, `:5852-5853`, throw `:5857`).
- `forTry` (base `:2019-2073`, now `:2019-2087`): the throw 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (base `:2029-2030`) is gone. After the catch clauses, which are unchanged, each type of the forbid clause is tested in turn, as a catch clause tests its type (`DUP`, `FException.getValue`, `InstantiatingClassloader.generalizedInstanceOf`, `IFEQ`); on a match the exception's value is passed to `throwForbiddenException`. The rethrow (`ATHROW`) and the label `done` move out of the `if (catchClauses.isSome())` block (`:2041`, `:2078-2081`) and are emitted when the try has a catch clause or a forbid clause, so a try with neither emits what it emitted before.
- `throwForbiddenException` (new, `:2089-2122`): with the exception's value on the stack, it finds `ForbiddenException`'s constructor in the api index of `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()` (the component's own index when it is that library), takes its parameter type and its result, casts the value to the parameter's class, calls the constructor's static method through `idToPackageClassAndName` and `NamingCzar.jvmMethodDesc`, as a source call of `ForbiddenException(e)` is emitted, wraps the result in an `FException` as `forThrow` does (`NEW`, `DUP_X1`, `SWAP`, `INVOKESPECIAL`) and throws it. The api's own types are named unqualified in its index, so the descriptor is made with the library's api as the default: with the program's api the first run asked for `ForbidClauseCompiled$ForbiddenException.class`, 'Resource not found'. The emitted call is the source call's, `invokestatic fortress/CompilerLibrary.ForbiddenException:(Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$Exception;)Lfortress/CompilerLibrary$ForbiddenException;` (by `javap -c -p` on the test's jar, the same instruction as a probe's source `throw ForbiddenException(e)` compiled on the base).
- `fnDeclCompilableModifiers` (base `:2897-2899`, now `:2947-2949`): `.combine(Modifiers.Test)`, so `forFnDecl`'s guard (`:3021`) passes a function declared `test`, which then compiles as the function it is. What `fortress test` runs is not changed.

Why: these are rows 820, 821 and 823, three of the code generator's 14 kinds over the library, each in one method (CLIMB-BATCH-25.md, fork 14; P-33); the specification gives each construct's meaning (the provenance lines), and walk runs all three (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:1401-1436`, `interpreter/evaluator/CollectTests.java:51`).

## 2. The tests, failing then passing

- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExtendsGenericAtAnyCompiled.fss`, `tests/ExtendsGenericAtAnyWalk.fss`: `trait Holder[\T extends Any\]` with `keep(x: T): T = x` and an abstract `describe()`, `object AnyHolder extends Holder[\Any\]`; asserts `describe()`, and that `keep` at `Any` keeps a `ZZ32` as a `ZZ32` and a `String` as a `String`.
- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ForbidClauseCompiled.fss`, `tests/ForbidClauseWalk.fss`: a body throwing `Boom` under `forbid Boom` reaches the caller as a `ForbiddenException` whose `chain` is `Boom`; `forbid { CheckedException, UncheckedException }` turns `Bang` into one; a catch clause that takes `Boom` takes it before `forbid Boom`; a catch clause of another type leaves `Boom` to `forbid Boom`; `Fizz`, of no listed type, passes on as `Fizz`; a body that completes normally ignores the clause. Each `try` with a forbid clause is in a function of its own and the caller catches (section 9, D7).
- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/TestModifierCompiled.fss`, `tests/TestModifierWalk.fss`: `test twiceOfTwo(): () = assert(twice(2), 4, ...)` beside a `run` that asserts `twice(3)` and does not call the test (tests.tex's note: a non-test must not refer to a test).

## 1. What changed, and why

Three changes in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, and one helper that the second needs, nothing else of the original tree:

- `generateTypeReference`, its `AnyType` branch (base `:5795-5796`, now `:5845-5851`): it was empty and fell through to the throw 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (base `:5802`). It now calls `generateTypeReference` with Any's own name, `NodeFactory.makeId(span, WellKnownNames.anyTypeLibrary(), WellKnownNames.anyTypeName)`, and no static arguments, and continues, as the `TraitType` branch does for a trait (`:5835-5837`). For a name without static arguments the method emits `GETSTATIC <its RTTI class>.ONLY` (`:5759-5767`), here `fortress/AnyType$Any$RTTIc.ONLY`, the field that the bootstrap class declares (`ProjectFortress/src/fortress/AnyType.java`, `RTTIc.ONLY`). The `BottomType`, `SelfType` and `AbbreviatedType` branches stay empty, each still ending in the throw (`:5833-5834`, `:5843-5844`, `:5852-5853`, throw `:5857`).
- `forTry` (base `:2019-2073`, now `:2019-2087`): the throw 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (base `:2029-2030`) is gone. After the catch clauses, which are unchanged, each type of the forbid clause is tested in turn, as a catch clause tests its type (`DUP`, `FException.getValue`, `InstantiatingClassloader.generalizedInstanceOf`, `IFEQ`); on a match the exception's value is passed to `throwForbiddenException`. The rethrow (`ATHROW`) and the label `done` move out of the `if (catchClauses.isSome())` block (`:2041`, `:2078-2081`) and are emitted when the try has a catch clause or a forbid clause, so a try with neither emits what it emitted before.
- `throwForbiddenException` (new, `:2089-2122`): with the exception's value on the stack, it finds `ForbiddenException`'s constructor in the api index of `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()` (the component's own index when it is that library), takes its parameter type and its result, casts the value to the parameter's class, calls the constructor's static method through `idToPackageClassAndName` and `NamingCzar.jvmMethodDesc`, as a source call of `ForbiddenException(e)` is emitted, wraps the result in an `FException` as `forThrow` does (`NEW`, `DUP_X1`, `SWAP`, `INVOKESPECIAL`) and throws it. The api's own types are named unqualified in its index, so the descriptor is made with the library's api as the default: with the program's api the first run asked for `ForbidClauseCompiled$ForbiddenException.class`, 'Resource not found'. The emitted call is the source call's, `invokestatic fortress/CompilerLibrary.ForbiddenException:(Lfortress/CompilerBuiltin$Exception;)Lfortress/CompilerLibrary$ForbiddenException;` (by `javap -c -p` on the test's jar, the same instruction as a probe's source `throw ForbiddenException(e)` compiled on the base).
- `fnDeclCompilableModifiers` (base `:2897-2899`, now `:2947-2949`): `.combine(Modifiers.Test)`, so `forFnDecl`'s guard (`:3021`) passes a function declared `test`, which then compiles as the function it is. What `fortress test` runs is not changed.

Why: these are rows 820, 821 and 823, three of the code generator's 14 kinds over the library, each in one method (CLIMB-BATCH-25.md, fork 14; P-33); the specification gives each construct's meaning (the provenance lines), and walk runs all three (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:1401-1436`, `interpreter/evaluator/CollectTests.java:51`).

# Rung C (`rung-codegen-walls`): record lines for the gather

Climb batch 25, rung C, on `wip/rung-codegen-walls`: the fix is `bc72d9dec`, its tests first in `511c18322`. `<C>` below stands for the landed commit of the fix. Detail and evidence: `compile-ladder/rung-codegen-walls/REPORT.md`, by section.

## Findings

1. **The code generator compiles a trait or object that extends a generic trait at the static argument `Any`.** Holds after `<C>`, for `Any` as a whole static argument of an `extends` entry. `generateTypeReference`'s `AnyType` branch emits Any's type reference, `GETSTATIC fortress/AnyType$Any$RTTIc.ONLY`, as for a trait without static arguments (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5845-5851`); on the base it fell to 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (`:5795-5802` at 97a416b18). Test: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExtendsGenericAtAnyCompiled.test` (link, run, PASS), walk guard `ProjectFortress/tests/ExtendsGenericAtAnyWalk.fss`. `Bottom`, `Self` and an abbreviated type as such an argument still fall to the throw (`:5843-5844`, `:5833-5834`, `:5852-5853`, not measured), and a tuple that holds `Any` crashes (finding 5). REPORT.md sections 1, 2.
2. **The code generator compiles a `try` with a `forbid` clause as the specification gives it.** Holds after `<C>`: an exception that the body throws and that no catch clause takes, of a type the clause lists or below it, is thrown on as a `ForbiddenException` whose `chain` is that exception; the catch clause takes first; an exception of no listed type passes on unchanged; a normal completion ignores the clause (`Specification/basic/expressions/try.tex:47-53`, `:56-81`; `Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:177-210`). `forTry` tests the forbid types after the catch clauses (`CodeGen.java:2064-2081`) and a new `throwForbiddenException` (`:2089-2122`) calls the library's constructor, found in the api index of `WellKnownNames.fortressLibrary()`, as a source call `ForbiddenException(e)` is emitted. Test: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ForbidClauseCompiled.test`, walk guard `ProjectFortress/tests/ForbidClauseWalk.fss`. A `try` with neither a catch nor a forbid clause emits what it emitted before. REPORT.md sections 1, 2.
3. **The code generator compiles a function declared with the modifier `test` as the function it is.** Holds after `<C>`: `fnDeclCompilableModifiers` holds `test` beside the getter, setter, `io`, `private` and `abstract` modifiers (`CodeGen.java:2947-2949`), so `forFnDecl`'s guard (`:3021`) passes it (on a method too, by reading; not run); what `fortress test` runs is unchanged. Test: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/TestModifierCompiled.test` (a `test` function beside `run`, compiled, linked and run), walk guard `ProjectFortress/tests/TestModifierWalk.fss`. `override` is still refused (row 650). REPORT.md sections 1, 2.
4. **On the compiled path a `try` nested in another `try` in one body is matched against the outer `try`'s catch clause first.** Holds on the base and after `<C>`: `forTry` writes its exception-table entry before it visits its body (`CodeGen.java:2032` at 97a416b18, `:2030` after), so the inner entry follows the outer one over the same range and the JVM takes the first that covers the throw. An exception both clauses take is caught by the outer one; one only the inner one takes leaves the body uncaught. Measured on the old code: a probe of the test's two functions printed 'outer', then 'FortressException: class NestedTryProbe$Boom with string Boom'; walk printed 'inner' twice. Test: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXNestedTryInnerCatch.test` with `NestedTryInnerCatchLink.test` (green: 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)'; red on a deliberate change: 'Did not see expected failure'), walk guard `ProjectFortress/tests/NestedTryInnerCatchWalk.fss`. For the work: a compiled `try` with a catch or forbid clause belongs in a function of its own when an enclosing `try` of the same body could take its exception; the one library's `shouldRaise` has none. NEW-C-1. REPORT.md sections 2, 5, 10.
5. **The code generator crashes with a `NullPointerException` on a trait or object whose `extends` clause gives a generic trait a tuple static argument that holds `Any`.** Holds on the base and after `<C>`, for `object PairHolder extends Holder[\(Any, ZZ32)\]`, which the checker accepts: `generateTypeReference`'s tuple branch passes an element that is neither a trait type nor a type variable back to itself with a null name (`CodeGen.java:5747` at 97a416b18, `:5797` after), and `NamingCzar.repairedApiName` dereferences it (`compiler/NamingCzar.java:1720`). # Rung C (`rung-codegen-walls`): the code generator's three walls: `Any` in an `extends` clause, `forbid`, and `test`

problem: under the switch-over's setting the code generator refused 50 declarations of the one library's fourteen components in 14 kinds, three of them in one method each of `CodeGen.java`: 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (`MIMapReduceReduction`, `TrivialOpenRange`; row 820), 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (`shouldRaise`; row 821) and 'Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl.' (`test stringifyChars`; row 823) (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-25.md:375-385; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5795-5796, :2029-2030, :2897-2899 at 97a416b18)
spec: a forbid clause throws "a new ForbiddenException ... with the thrown exception as its argument", the catch clause first (Specification/basic/expressions/try.tex:56-81), the same as a catch clause that throws ForbiddenException(e) (Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:177-210); an extends clause names any instance of a generic trait, Any among the static arguments (Specification/basic/traits.tex, "Trait Declarations"); the test modifier on a top-level function (Specification/basic/tests.tex:36-55, its note)
precedent: the IntArg branch of the same `generateTypeReference`, which repaired the same message for a size (row 411, e893a3e00; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5863-5873); `forTry`'s own catch-clause loop and `forThrow` (:2047-2063, :2006-2017); the source call of a library constructor (`functionalRefToPackageClassAndMethod`, `resolveMethodAndSignature`, :3841-3857, :1492-1515); the trait guard that already holds `test` (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/Modifiers.java:146-147)
deviation: the AnyType branch builds Any's name (`AnyType.Any`) and calls `generateTypeReference`, where the TraitType branch passes the trait type's own name (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5845-5851); the ForbiddenException call is emitted by a new private helper, `throwForbiddenException`, which finds the constructor in the library's api index, as no source call names it (:2089-2122); the guard admits `test` on methods as well as on top-level functions, where the specification's note speaks of top-level functions (:2947-2949); nothing else departs from the specification's spelling (none)
historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java (the team's sites at a874948ac: `forTry`'s throw :2013-2014, the guard :2866-2868, the AnyType branch :5753-5754)

## 1. What changed, and why

Three changes in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, and one helper that the second needs, nothing else of the original tree:

- `generateTypeReference`, its `AnyType` branch (base `:5795-5796`, now `:5845-5851`): it was empty and fell through to the throw 'Only handling some static args of generic types in extends clause' (base `:5802`). It now calls `generateTypeReference` with Any's own name, `NodeFactory.makeId(span, WellKnownNames.anyTypeLibrary(), WellKnownNames.anyTypeName)`, and no static arguments, and continues, as the `TraitType` branch does for a trait (`:5835-5837`). For a name without static arguments the method emits `GETSTATIC <its RTTI class>.ONLY` (`:5759-5767`), here `fortress/AnyType$Any$RTTIc.ONLY`, the field that the bootstrap class declares (`ProjectFortress/src/fortress/AnyType.java`, `RTTIc.ONLY`). The `BottomType`, `SelfType` and `AbbreviatedType` branches stay empty, each still ending in the throw (`:5833-5834`, `:5843-5844`, `:5852-5853`, throw `:5857`).
- `forTry` (base `:2019-2073`, now `:2019-2087`): the throw 'NYI: Forbid clauses are not yet implemented' (base `:2029-2030`) is gone.
